svg.title: Victorian London Public Health (1854–75): John Snow's Soho Investigation and Bazalgette's Sewers
svg.desc: Two-panel historical GIS atlas map: Panel A shows a real WGS84 street plan of Soho in September 1854 plotting Dr John Snow's Broad Street water pump [51.5133°N, -0.1366°W], No. 40 Broad Street cesspit, Lion Brewery (0 deaths), St James's Workhouse on Poland Street (5 deaths / 535 inmates), and the Hampstead Susannah Eley outlier; Panel B shows Metropolitan London boroughs and the tidal River Thames contrasting the dirty Battersea vs clean Thames Ditton water intakes (Snow's Grand Experiment) alongside Sir Joseph Bazalgette's 1,300-mile intercepting sewer network to Abbey Mills and Crossness (1858–1875).

text.tspan: ① Broad St Water Pump (8 Sept 1854)
Handle Removed • No. 40 Cesspit 3 ft Away

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 1 (OPTION 11): MEDICINE IN BRITAIN, c1250–PRESENT
Victorian London Public Health (1854–75): Snow’s Soho Map & Bazalgette’s Sewers
Snow’s 1854 Soho spot map & South London water comparison proved cholera was waterborne—yet officials clung to miasma until the 1860s.
The 1858 Great Stink forced Parliament to fund Bazalgette’s sewers; 1861 Germ Theory & 1867 working-class vote drove the compulsory 1875 Act.
